_scenario: Keep-out zones, built so the controller wants to fly through them. One quadrotor is pinned through an identity map to a horizontal orbit of radius 1.8 m about the origin, and that circle passes exactly through the axis of the 'pillar' column at [1.8, 0] and exactly through the centre of the 'net' sphere at [-1.8, 0, 1.4]. One rover is pinned through PROJECT_XY to a waypoint lane that runs straight along y = 0 from x = -2.5 to x = 4.5 and back, straight through the same pillar. The sheaf has no objection to any of this: both agents have a global section of their own and both sections intersect solid geometry. Nothing in the gradient flow knows the obstacles exist, which is the point -- the CBF filter is the only thing between the command and the pillar.
_what_each_zone_shows: The pillar is a cylinder with applies=all: a column measured on HORIZONTAL distance over the z span [0.0, 2.5], so it constrains the quadrotor at 1.4 m and the rover at 0.1 m alike, and would constrain neither above 2.75 m (the span plus the 0.25 m switch-on pad). The net is a sphere with applies=air, measured in R^3: it turns the quadrotor away, and the rover drives under it untouched even though it passes 1.30 m from the centre, inside the 1.5 m radius. Change applies to 'all' and the rover is turned away too -- that one field is the whole difference.
_how_to_run: Start the server on this config, drive it with scripts/fake_sim.py --csv, and read the minimum distance from each zone centre out of the CSV. Run it once with the keep_out list present and once with it deleted (or with SHEAF_CBF=0) to see the difference. fake_sim's own RESULT line is not the verdict here, for the same reason it is not in config/collide.json: with no consensus edges the consensus residual is identically zero, so its converging test has nothing to compare, and an agent held off a zone is supposed to carry a nonzero tracking residual.
